- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5 days.
- Model tends to lag in correcting for recent sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns from positive to negative; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00s), model often overfits to recent highs; cap forecast at 1–2% below the 18-day moving average to avoid over-optimism.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 18-day average, adjust forecast to reflect mean reversion toward historical volatility bands — especially if sentiment is flat or negative.
